mainTopic: Is a טומטום a doubtful male or female? Telling the gender of a טומטום animal, the principle 'since it has changed, it has changed,' and יבום with the wife of a טומטום.
overview: The גמרא first shows that everyone agrees a טומטום is really male or female, not a separate creature. The real argument is about a טומטום animal that urinates from the female place. The רבנן worry its male organ may be turned inward, while רבי שמעון בן יהודה does not, matching רבי אלעזר's ruling that such an animal is חולין. רבי יוחנן objects that רבי אלעזר follows one opinion, the רבנן בתראי, against two. The גמרא explains that רבי אלעזר relies on ריש לקיש: in an animal, unlike a person, the place of urination shows whether it is male or female. רב אושעיא asks whether we should worry the organ was flipped. One answer ties that worry to רבי מאיר. Another says even the רבנן might worry, because 'since it has changed, it has changed.' The גמרא then tests whether two ברייתות about יבום with a טומטום's wife argue about this principle. It concludes that they really follow רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, with the רבי עקיבא ברייתא matching רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who treats a טומטום as only a possible סריס חמה. The amud ends by asking how רבי יהודה and his son differ in practice, and רבא's answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: So רבי שמעון בן יהודה would hold a טומטום is a separate creature
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its suggestion: רבי שמעון בן יהודה would hold that a טומטום is its own kind of creature, so it is never holy as a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן יהודה comes to say that a טומטום is a separate creature and is not holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the sentence that started at the end of the previous amud. It is proposing that the תנאים argue: the חכמים call a טומטום a ספק, while רבי שמעון בן יהודה holds it is a separate creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a טומטום were a separate creature, neither male nor female, it could never be a בכור, which must be male. If that is רבי שמעון בן יהודה's view, then whether a טומטום is a ספק or a separate creature would be an argument between תנאים. The next step rejects this.

keyTerms.meaning: a creature whose private area is covered, so we cannot tell if it is male or female
a creature of its own kind, a separate category
holy, here meaning it has the holiness of a בכור

phrases.english: [and רבי שמעון] בן יהודה comes to say:
phrases.notes: This sentence starts at the end of the previous amud, with the first part of רבי שמעון בן יהודה's name.

phrases.english: a טומטום is a separate creature, and it is not holy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the suggestion of the previous amud's last step, that the תנאים argue about a טומטום.
steps.raayaObject: That whether a טומטום is a ספק or a separate creature is an argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון בן יהודה's statement that a טומטום is a separate creature and is not holy.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the only doubt is male or female
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says no. All agree a טומטום is not a separate creature. The only question is whether it is male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees there is no doubt that a טומטום is not a separate creature. The doubt is only whether it is male or female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 1. Both sides here agree that a טומטום is not its own category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the whole argument. A טומטום really is either male or female; we just cannot see which. So any disagreement must be about how we decide which one it is.

keyTerms.meaning: everyone agrees
is in doubt
male and female

phrases.english: No, for everyone agrees:
about a טומטום being a separate creature, there is no doubt,
phrases.notes: He means there is no doubt that it is NOT a separate creature.

phrases.english: it is male or female that is in doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed proof in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the תנאים argue about whether a טומטום is a separate creature.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No one holds a טומטום is a separate creature; the only doubt is whether it is male or female.

steps.title: The real argument: urinating from the female place
steps.stepSummary: If it urinates from the male place, all agree it is male. They argue when it urinates from the female place: the רבנן worry the male organ may be turned inward; רבי שמעון בן יהודה does not worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it urinates from the male place, everyone agrees it is male. They argue about one that urinates from the female place. One opinion worries that maybe the male organ is turned toward the female place. The other opinion does not worry about that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps answering and now shows exactly where the two sides disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Urinating from the male place proves it is male. Urinating from the female place could mean it is female, or it could be a male whose organ is turned inward. The רבנן keep that worry, so it stays a ספק. רבי שמעון בן יהודה does not worry about it, so it is simply female.

keyTerms.meaning: urinates
the male organ / the female organ
we are concerned, we take the possibility into account
was turned over or turned inward

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees a טומטום is either male or female. The argument is only about whether urinating from the female place proves it is female.

phrases.english: If it urinates from the place of the male organ,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּזָכָר הוּא,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that it is male.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּמֵטִיל מַיִם בְּמָקוֹם נַקְבוּת:
phrases.english: Where they argue is when it urinates from the place of the female organ:
One master holds that we are concerned
phrases.notes: This first master is the רבנן, and the second one is רבי שמעון בן יהודה.

phrases.english: that perhaps its male organ was turned toward its female place,
and the other master holds that we are not concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer by pinpointing the case the two sides argue about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue only when it urinates from the female place: worry that the organ is turned inward, or no such worry.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר rules like the side that does not worry
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ruled that an animal that urinates from the female place is חולין, matching רבי שמעון בן יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי אלעזר ruled: an animal that urinates from the female place is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the 'no worry' opinion matches a practical ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר treats such an animal as definitely female, so it cannot be a בכור and is plain חולין. This is exactly the view that does not worry about a turned-in male organ. It also sets up רבי יוחנן's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: ruled, gave a practical halachic ruling
an animal
not holy, ordinary

phrases.english: Like that which Rabbi Elazar ruled:
an animal that urinates from the place of the female organ
is not holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the 'no worry' opinion from step 3 to a real ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The 'no worry' opinion of רבי שמעון בן יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's ruling that such an animal is חולין.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is puzzled by רבי אלעזר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן wonders who would rule this way and ignore the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל, who treat a טומטום as a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן wondered: who ignores the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling. He asks how one can ignore two opinions in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל treat a טומטום as a ספק. By ruling it is surely female and חולין, רבי אלעזר seems to brush both of them aside. That is the core of רבי יוחנן's surprise.

keyTerms.meaning: wondered about it, was puzzled
is not concerned for, ignores
the first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan wondered about it:
Who is it that is not concerned for the first Tanna
and for Rabbi Yishmael?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling brought in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that the animal is חולין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling goes against the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל, who both treat a טומטום as a doubt.

steps.title: Why not mention the later Sages too, based on רב חסדא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not also say רבי אלעזר ignores the רבנן בתראי. According to רב חסדא, they also treat a טומטום as a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי יוחנן also say: who ignores the later Sages? For רב חסדא said: the argument is about an אנדרוגינוס, but about a טומטום everyone agrees it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how רבי יוחנן worded his challenge. It says his challenge could have been even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא teaches that the רבנן בתראי argue only about an אנדרוגינוס, and they too call a טומטום a ספק. If so, רבי אלעזר goes against three opinions, not two. So why did רבי יוחנן list only two?

keyTerms.meaning: the later Sages, the last opinion in the משנה
a creature with both male and female organs
all opinions agree
a doubt, a case of uncertainty

phrases.english: But let Rabbi Yochanan also say:
Who is it that is not concerned for the later Sages?
For Rav Chisda said:
The argument is about an androginos,
but about a טומטום, everyone agrees it is a doubt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רבי יוחנן's challenge in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן listing only two opinions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב חסדא, the רבנן בתראי also treat a טומטום as a ספק, so רבי יוחנן should have listed three opinions.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן does not agree with רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן does not hold like רב חסדא, so for him the רבנן בתראי are not on that list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן does not agree with רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 6. רבי יוחנן reads the רבנן בתראי differently from רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רב חסדא's reading, the רבנן בתראי hold that a טומטום, too, is a separate creature (Rashi), not a ספק. So רבי יוחנן could list only two opinions that רבי אלעזר goes against.

keyTerms.meaning: he does not hold this view

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan does not hold like Rav Chisda.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise: the questioner relied on רב חסדא, and רבי יוחנן does not accept him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן should have counted the רבנן בתראי as a third opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוחנן, the רבנן בתראי do not treat a טומטום as a ספק, so only two opinions are against רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Then רבי אלעזר simply follows the later Sages
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן does not agree with רב חסדא, then רבי אלעזר has a source in the רבנן בתראי. So why was רבי יוחנן puzzled at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he does not agree with רב חסדא, let him say that רבי אלעזר ruled like the later Sages!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer of step 7 into a new problem. Now רבי יוחנן's surprise seems to have no reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the רבנן בתראי are not on the ספק side, רבי אלעזר has a source to rely on. So רבי יוחנן's original question, 'who ignores the others?', seems to have an easy answer: the רבנן בתראי.

keyTerms.meaning: if
let him say

phrases.english: If he does not hold like him,
let him say that he ruled like the later Sages?
phrases.notes: The 'he' who ruled is רבי אלעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new challenge from the answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's original puzzlement in step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רבנן בתראי do not treat a טומטום as a ספק, then רבי אלעזר clearly follows them, and there is nothing to wonder about.

steps.title: How can you leave two opinions and follow one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this was רבי יוחנן's point all along: רבי אלעזר left the two opinions that call it a doubt and followed the single opinion of the רבנן בתראי.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is indeed what he is saying: who leaves two opinions and acts like one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real meaning of רבי יוחנן's question. He knew רבי אלעזר follows the רבנן בתראי; his surprise was about following one opinion against two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's question was never 'who is your source?' It was 'why follow one opinion against two others?' Normally a single opinion against two is not the one we rule by, so his surprise makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: that is indeed what he is saying
leaves two and acts like one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's question means: רבי אלעזר follows the רבנן בתראי alone and goes against the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל. Why rule like one against two?

phrases.english: That is indeed what he is saying:
Who leaves two and acts like one!
phrases.notes: The two are the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל; the one is the later Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by explaining what רבי יוחנן's question in step 5 really meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was asking who could be רבי אלעזר's source.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן knew the source was the רבנן בתראי. He was puzzled that רבי אלעזר followed one opinion against two.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעזר's ruling follows the רבנן בתראי alone. רבי יוחנן objects to ruling like one opinion against two.

steps.title: What is רבי אלעזר's reasoning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which reasoning or opinion רבי אלעזר is following.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose view does רבי אלעזר follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks what reasoning stands behind רבי אלעזר's ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן assumed that רבי אלעזר follows only the רבנן בתראי. Now the גמרא asks what רבי אלעזר himself relied on. The answer will show that for an animal his ruling can fit every opinion, because in an animal there is no doubt at all (Rashi).

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does he follow?
A person or animal whose private parts are covered, so we cannot see whether it is male or female

phrases.english: And רבי אלעזר, in accordance with whom does he hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יוחנן's objection that רבי אלעזר follows one opinion against two, the גמרא asks what רבי אלעזר actually relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning that lets רבי אלעזר treat a טומטום animal as clearly male or female.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a טומטום is only a doubt in humans
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר follows ריש לקיש. A טומטום is a doubt only in a person, because in a person both organs are in the same place. In an animal they are in different places, so where it urinates shows whether it is male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like ריש לקיש said: they called a טומטום a doubt only in a person, since the male and female organs are in one place. But in an animal, if it urinates from the male place it is male, and if from the female place it is female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר holds like ריש לקיש. A טומטום animal is not really a doubt, because we can tell its gender by where it urinates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a human, both organs are in the same area, so when that area is covered we cannot know. In an animal the male and female openings are in different spots. So even if the organ is covered, the place the urine comes from tells us the gender. According to Rashi, this means that in an animal there is no doubt according to anyone, so רבי אלעזר's ruling fits all the opinions, and רבי יוחנן's objection falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt, an unclear case
The male organ
The female organ
Urinates

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic idea behind רבי אלעזר's view, and the next steps challenge and defend it.

phrases.english: Like that which ריש לקיש said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמְרוּ טוּמְטוּם סָפֵק אֶלָּא בְּאָדָם,
phrases.english: They said a טומטום is a doubt only with a person,
since his male and female organs are in one place,
but an animal:
if it urinates from the place of the male organ, it is male;
if it urinates from the place of the female organ, it is female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 by supplying ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר follows ריש לקיש. A טומטום animal can be identified by where it urinates, because an animal's male and female organs are in different places.

steps.title: רב אושעיא: maybe the organ was flipped
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא objects: maybe this animal's male organ was turned around to the place of the female organ, so the urine test cannot be trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא challenged it: let us worry that maybe its male organ was flipped to the female place!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא attacks ריש לקיש's test. Maybe the organs in this animal are not in their normal places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's test only works if the organs sit where they usually do. If the male organ could be turned toward the female spot, then urine from the 'female' place would not prove it is female. So the doubt would return.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, raised a strong objection
And let us worry
Was turned around, flipped

phrases.english: רב אושעיא challenged it:
But let us worry that perhaps its male organ was turned to its female place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reliability of ריש לקיש's urine test from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that where the animal urinates shows its gender.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the organs could be out of place, the location of urination proves nothing, and the טומטום animal would still be a doubt.

steps.title: That worry follows רבי מאיר, who worries about rare cases
steps.stepSummary: The reply: your worry follows רבי מאיר, who takes rare cases into account. We do not rule that way, so we follow what is normal in animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: according to whom? According to רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority?!
steps.whatsHappening: The answer pushes back on רב אושעיא. A flipped organ is rare, and only רבי מאיר worries about rare cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most animals do not have flipped organs. The רבנן follow the majority and ignore rare possibilities. Only רבי מאיר worries about the minority, so רב אושעיא's question only works according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Worries about the minority, takes rare cases into account

phrases.english: He said to him: according to whom?
According to רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ כְּמַאן כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּחָיֵישׁ לְמִיעוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אושעיא's objection by tying it to a minority view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the objection to a view we do not follow (רבי מאיר).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We must worry that the organ is flipped, so the urine test fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: A flipped organ is a rare case. Since we follow the majority, the urine test stands.

steps.title: Even the רבנן might worry: once it has changed, it has changed
steps.stepSummary: אביי בר אבין and רב חנניא בר אבין say רב אושעיא's worry can fit even the רבנן. An animal that is already unusual may be unusual in other ways too. This idea is itself debated.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי בר אבין and רב חנניא בר אבין both said: you can even say it follows the רבנן, because since it has changed, it has changed. Some say it has changed, and some say it has not changed.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים defend רב אושעיא's question even according to the רבנן. They point out that this is not a normal animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of following the majority works when the animal is like most animals. A טומטום is already different from normal animals, so maybe its organs are also out of place. Not everyone accepts this idea: some say 'it has changed', and some say it has not. Rashi explains that this also answers רב אושעיא: the תנא קמא of the ברייתא, who worried the organ was turned, holds 'it has changed,' while רבי אלעזר follows רבי שמעון בן יהודה, who holds it has not.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the רבנן
Since it has changed (in one way), it has changed (in other ways too)
There are those who say

steps.confusionAlert: This is not רבי מאיר's worry about rare cases coming back. The רבנן still follow the majority. The point is that a טומטום is not part of the normal majority to begin with.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חֲנַנְיָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: אביי בר אבין and רב חנניא בר אבין
both of them say:
You may even say it follows the רבנן,
since it has changed, it has changed.
phrases.notes: The animal is already unusual because it is a טומטום, so maybe its organs are unusual too.

phrases.english: There are those who say it has changed,
and there are those who say it has not changed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן הוֹאִיל וְאִישְׁתַּנִּי אִישְׁתַּנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 13's claim that רב אושעיא's worry belongs only to רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רב אושעיא's objection works only according to רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Following the majority does not settle an animal that is already unusual. Once it has changed in one way, it may have changed in another. The question becomes a dispute over this principle.

steps.title: Is 'it has changed' a dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the debate over 'since it has changed, it has changed' may already be a dispute between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that 'it has changed' and 'it has not changed' is a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the debate from the last step goes back to the תנאים. This sets up a ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 ended with two views: some say 'it has changed' and some say it has not. Now the גמרא wonders whether earlier תנאים already argued about the same idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? A suggestion the גמרא will test
A dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Shall we say that 'it has changed' and 'it has not changed' is a dispute of תנאים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the dispute named in step 14 and asks whether it matches an earlier dispute of תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the principle 'since it has changed, it has changed' is argued about by תנאים.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a טומטום's קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא. If a טומטום betroths a woman, the betrothal counts. If a טומטום is betrothed by a man, the betrothal also counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: a טומטום who betrothed, his betrothal is a betrothal. If he was betrothed, his betrothal is a betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the ברייתא it will use to test its suggestion. The quote continues past this point, so this is still setup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a טומטום might be male, a betrothal he gives counts out of doubt. Because he might be female, a betrothal he receives also counts out of doubt. How this connects to 'it has changed' will become clear as the ברייתא continues.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Was betrothed (received קידושין)

phrases.english: As it was taught: a טומטום who betrothed a woman:
his betrothal is a betrothal,
if he was betrothed by a man, his betrothal is a betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the suggestion raised in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The suggestion that 'since it has changed, it has changed' is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the קידושין of a טומטום (the quote continues beyond this point).

steps.title: Two teachings that disagree about the wife of a טומטום
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא continues: a טומטום does חליצה, and his brothers may do either חליצה or יבום with his wife. A second ברייתא says his wife does חליצה but not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first ברייתא goes on: the טומטום can do חליצה, and his brothers can do חליצה or יבום with his wife. But another ברייתא teaches: the wife of a טומטום does חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא it started quoting and then sets a second ברייתא next to it. This lays out the evidence for the suggested dispute between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא treats the wife of a טומטום as fully fit for יבום. The second allows only חליצה, which means it has some doubt about whether she may do יבום. The גמרא will now try to explain the reason behind this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases a childless widow from her husband's brother so she does not need יבום
Marriage of a childless widow to her late husband's brother
A person whose gender cannot be seen because the organs are covered

phrases.english: And he performs chalitza, and they perform chalitza with his wife,
phrases.notes: "He" is the טומטום, if his brother dies childless. "They" are the טומטום's brothers, after the טומטום dies.

phrases.english: and they may do yibum with his wife.
And another baraita teaches:
The wife of a טומטום performs chalitza
but does not do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 16 and adds a second, opposing ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of 'since it has changed, it has changed' is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות that disagree about whether the wife of a טומטום may do יבום

steps.title: Assuming both teachings follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes that both ברייתות agree with רבי עקיבא, who says a סריס חמה does not do חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that everyone holds like רבי עקיבא, who says that a man who was a סריס from birth does not do חליצה or יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a shared starting point for both ברייתות. This prepares the next move, where it explains what they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both sides agree that a סריס חמה is completely outside יבום, their argument cannot be about that rule. It must be about whether we suspect that a טומטום might be a סריס חמה.

keyTerms.meaning: They assumed (a working assumption the גמרא may later reject)
A man who is unable to have children from birth
Everyone, meaning both sides of the dispute

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as the final ruling. סברוה introduces only a working assumption, and in step 20 the גמרא drops it, assigning one ברייתא to רבי אליעזר instead.

phrases.english: They assumed that everyone holds like Rabbi Akiva,
who says: a eunuch from birth
does not perform chalitza and does not do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a shared assumption that both ברייתות from step 17 are said to agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both ברייתות are assumed to hold that a סריס חמה is left out of חליצה and יבום.

steps.title: The suggestion that the teachings argue about 'since it changed, it changed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא that allows יבום does not say הואיל ואשתני אשתני. The ברייתא that allows only חליצה does say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this? The one who says the טומטום does חליצה, and his brothers do חליצה or יבום with his wife, does not say 'since he changed, he changed.' The one who says his wife does חליצה but not יבום does say 'since he changed, he changed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers its proof that the question from step 15 is already a dispute between תנאים. It reads each ברייתא as taking one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טומטום is already unusual. According to the second ברייתא, we therefore also worry that he may be a סריס חמה, whose wife may not do יבום, so she does only חליצה. The first ברייתא does not worry about this extra unusual feature, so his wife may do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that... (introduces a suggested reading)
They argue
Since it has changed, it has changed. Something already unusual may be unusual in other ways too.

steps.whyThisMatters: If this reading holds, the debate between אביי בר אבין and רב חנניא בר אבין and the other side is not new. It would go back to the תנאים.

phrases.english: Is it not that they argue about this:
that the one who says he performs chalitza,
and they perform chalitza with his wife or do yibum with his wife,
holds that we do not say
'since he changed, he changed';
phrases.notes: He means: since the טומטום is already unusual, maybe he is also a סריס חמה.

phrases.english: and the one who says she performs chalitza but not yibum,
holds that we do say 'since he changed, he changed'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the assumption from step 18 to explain why the two ברייתות in step 17 disagree.
steps.raayaObject: That הואיל ואשתני אשתני is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two ברייתות about the wife of a טומטום, read as following רבי עקיבא

steps.title: Both ברייתות agree; the dispute is רבי אליעזר versus רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the ברייתות argue about הואיל ואשתני אשתני. Everyone accepts that rule. One ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר and the other follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone says, 'Since he has changed, he has changed.' This ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, and that ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion from step 19. It says the two ברייתות do not argue about הואיל ואשתני אשתני at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that a טומטום is unusual enough that he might be a סריס חמה. They disagree about the law of a סריס חמה itself. The ברייתא that allows יבום follows רבי אליעזר, who allows יבום for a סריס חמה's wife. The ברייתא that allows only חליצה follows רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone; all opinions agree
Since he has changed, he has changed. Because the טומטום is already unusual in one way, we worry he may be unusual in another way too, such as being a סריס חמה.

steps.confusionAlert: Step 18 assumed that both ברייתות follow רבי עקיבא. This דחיה drops that assumption. Now only one ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: No, everyone says
since he has changed, he has changed;
this one is רבי אליעזר,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that lets the brothers do יבום with the טומטום's wife.

phrases.english: and that one is רבי עקיבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 19's claim that the ברייתות argue about הואיל ואשתני אשתני. It gives a different explanation of their disagreement.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects the claim that this is a dispute between תנאים about הואיל ואשתני אשתני.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The difference between the ברייתות can be explained by the known dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא about a סריס חמה. So the ברייתות need not argue about הואיל ואשתני אשתני.

steps.title: Which תנא follows רבי עקיבא here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the תנא is that follows רבי עקיבא and still requires חליצה for a טומטום's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who holds like רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move. It wants to identify the תנא of the ברייתא that requires חליצה but not יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, a definite סריס חמה's wife needs neither חליצה nor יבום. Since this ברייתא does require חליצה, its תנא must treat a טומטום as only possibly a סריס חמה. The גמרא wants to know who holds that view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא? This asks who holds the view in question.
According to; following the view of

phrases.english: And who is the תנא who follows רבי עקיבא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 20, which assigned one ברייתא to רבי עקיבא. Now the גמרא asks which תנא that ברייתא actually represents.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא follows רבי עקיבא on סריס חמה and also treats a טומטום as only a doubtful סריס, so that his wife needs חליצה?

steps.title: It cannot be רבי יהודה, who treats a טומטום as a definite סריס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules out רבי יהודה. He treats a טומטום who was opened and found male as a definite סריס, so his wife would need no חליצה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is רבי יהודה, he treats a טומטום as a definite סריס! As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, a טומטום who was torn open and found to be male does not do חליצה, because he is like a סריס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible answer, רבי יהודה, and shows that it does not fit. It brings a משנה as proof of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats such a טומטום as a definite סריס. According to רבי עקיבא, the wife of a definite סריס חמה needs neither יבום nor חליצה. But our ברייתא requires חליצה, so it cannot follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. This introduces a suggested answer that is about to be rejected.
A definite סריס, not a doubtful one
He treats him as; he considers him
Was torn open. The skin covering the טומטום's body was opened.

phrases.english: If you say it is רבי יהודה,
he treats him as a definite סריס!
As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says:
A טומטום who was torn open and found to be male
does not do חליצה,
because he is like a סריס!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a first candidate for the question in step 21 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יהודה is the תנא of the ברייתא requiring חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה treats a טומטום as a definite סריס. Following רבי עקיבא, the wife of a definite סריס חמה needs no חליצה. That contradicts the ברייתא, which requires חליצה.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He treats a טומטום as only possibly a סריס חמה, so his wife needs חליצה but not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. As it was taught: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says, a טומטום does not do חליצה, because perhaps he will be torn open and found to be a סריס חמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 21. The תנא is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, and it quotes a ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'perhaps' (שֶׁמָּא) shows that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה treats a טומטום as only possibly a סריס חמה. Because of that doubt, his wife needs חליצה, but she cannot do יבום. This matches the ברייתא that follows רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps. This signals a doubt, not a certainty.
A person born unable to have children, from birth or by nature

steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות accept הואיל ואשתני אשתני. The one allowing יבום follows רבי אליעזר. The one requiring only חליצה follows רבי עקיבא, as understood by רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who treats a טומטום as a doubtful סריס חמה. רבי יהודה treats him as a definite סריס.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יהודה with his son רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. The father treats a טומטום as a definite סריס. The son treats him as only a possible one.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Rather, it is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says:
A טומטום does not do חליצה,
because perhaps he will be torn open and found to be a סריס חמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי יהודה in step 22, the גמרא gives the correct answer to step 21's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He treats a טומטום as only possibly a סריס חמה, which explains why his wife needs חליצה but not יבום.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a ברייתא can follow רבי עקיבא and still require חליצה. The טומטום is only a doubtful סריס, not a definite one.

steps.title: Couldn't the opened טומטום turn out to be female?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. It asks why the only worry is סריס חמה, as if every opened טומטום must be male.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that every טומטום who is torn open is found to be male, and is never found to be female?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the reason just given for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. The reason mentioned only one worry, that he might be a סריס חמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worrying about a סריס חמה assumes the טומטום is a male. But a טומטום has hidden organs, so when opened he could just as easily turn out to be female. So why does the explanation speak only about סריס חמה?

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a challenge that exposes a strange assumption)
is torn open (the skin covering the טומטום's organs is cut)
male
female
is found to be

phrases.english: Is that to say that every one who is torn open
is found to be a male,
and is not found to be a female?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 23 for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's only concern is that the טומטום may be a סריס חמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That concern assumes the טומטום is male, but an opened טומטום could also be found female, so the explanation leaves out an obvious possibility.

steps.title: 'Perhaps' covers two doubts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה used the word 'perhaps,' which includes two doubts: maybe he is female, and even if male, maybe he is a סריס חמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it with the word 'perhaps': perhaps he will be torn open and found to be female. Or, even if he is male, perhaps he will be found to be a סריס חמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה by showing that his 'perhaps' was never only about one worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two layers of doubt. First, the טומטום might be female. Second, even if he is male, he might be a סריס חמה. Both doubts stand together, so the female possibility was already included.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps (introduces a doubt)
he is saying
or alternatively
a eunuch from birth, by nature (not by human action)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, a טומטום is a double doubt: maybe female, and even if male, maybe a סריס חמה.

phrases.english: He said "perhaps":
phrases.notes: His word 'perhaps' was meant to hold more than one doubt.

phrases.english: perhaps he will be torn open and found to be a female.
Or, even if he is a male,
perhaps he will be found to be a סריס חמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: 'perhaps' includes several doubts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה only worried about סריס חמה, ignoring the chance that the טומטום is female.
steps.terutzMaskana: He worried about both: maybe female, and even if male, maybe a סריס חמה.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, and introduces רבא to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them? רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the two opinions differ in practice, and is setting up רבא's answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats the opened טומטום as a definite סריס, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה treats him as only a doubtful one. Both of them say he does not do חליצה (Rashi), so the גמרא wants to know in what real case this difference would change the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (asks for the practical outcome of a dispute)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After clarifying רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view, the גמרא compares it with רבי יהודה's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case where רבי יהודה (definite סריס) and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (doubtful סריס) would rule differently.
